test_cases.title: Sample Throughput Sustains 20 Hz
test_cases.setup: Initialize the barometric altimeter library with a POSIX mock device that returns synthetic samples on demand. Use a mocked clock advancing in 50 ms increments.
procedure: Initialize the library via its New/Init entry point.
In a loop, advance the mock clock by 50 ms and invoke the library read interface to retrieve a sample.
Record the timestamp associated with each returned sample over a 2-second window (40 samples).
Compute the inter-sample interval between consecutive returned samples.
Verify that the library accepts the 20 Hz call cadence and returns one fresh sample per call.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The library returns 40 samples over the 2-second window with mean inter-sample interval of 50 ms +/- 1 ms and no dropped samples reported.

test_cases.title: Pressure Reported in Pascals
test_cases.setup: Initialize the library with a POSIX mock device configured to return a known raw pressure register value corresponding to 101325 Pa (standard sea-level pressure).
procedure: Inject a raw pressure register pattern equivalent to 101325 Pa into the mock device.
Invoke the library read interface to retrieve a sample.
Read the pressure field from the returned sample structure.
Repeat with a second injected value corresponding to 90000 Pa and verify the conversion.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Pressure field equals 101325 Pa +/- 1 Pa for the first injection and 90000 Pa +/- 1 Pa for the second injection; field unit and scale documented as pascals.

test_cases.title: Temperature Reported in Degrees Celsius
test_cases.setup: Initialize the library with a POSIX mock device configured to return a known raw temperature register value corresponding to 25.0 degrees C.
procedure: Inject a raw temperature register pattern equivalent to 25.0 degrees C into the mock device.
Invoke the library read interface to retrieve a sample.
Read the temperature field from the returned sample structure.
Repeat with a second injected value corresponding to -10.0 degrees C and verify the conversion.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Temperature field equals 25.0 degrees C +/- 0.1 degrees C for the first injection and -10.0 degrees C +/- 0.1 degrees C for the second injection.

test_cases.title: Derived Altitude Reported in Meters
test_cases.setup: Initialize the library with a POSIX mock device configured to return raw values corresponding to 101325 Pa (sea-level reference, 0 m) and 25.0 degrees C.
procedure: Inject raw register values corresponding to 101325 Pa into the mock device.
Invoke the library read interface to retrieve a sample.
Read the altitude field from the returned sample structure.
Inject raw register values corresponding to 89876 Pa (approx 1000 m above the reference) and re-read.
Verify the altitude field tracks the pressure change in meters.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Altitude field reads 0 m +/- 1 m at sea-level pressure and approximately 1000 m +/- 5 m at the elevated injection pressure; field unit documented as meters.

test_cases.title: POST Reports Device Present
test_cases.setup: Flight Pico 2 board with MPL3115A2 altimeter wired to the configured I2C bus. Serial console open at 115200 baud capturing boot output.
procedure: Power on the flight board with the MPL3115A2 altimeter connected.
Capture the boot serial output containing the POST report.
Locate the barometric altimeter POST line in the captured output.
Power off the board, disconnect the altimeter, and power on again.
Capture the second boot serial output.
Locate the barometric altimeter POST line in the second capture.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: First boot POST line indicates barometric altimeter present and responsive; second boot POST line (device removed) indicates barometric altimeter absent or non-responsive.

expected_artifacts.description: Serial capture of boot POST output with altimeter connected

expected_artifacts.description: Serial capture of boot POST output with altimeter disconnected

test_cases.title: Health Indicator Reflects Sample Flow
test_cases.setup: Initialize the library with a POSIX mock device. Provide a mocked clock and a control to enable or stall mock sample production.
procedure: Configure the mock to produce fresh samples on each read; advance the clock and call the read interface several times at 20 Hz cadence.
Query the library health indicator and record its value.
Configure the mock to stop producing fresh samples (stall reads or return stale data).
Continue advancing the clock past the configured staleness threshold and call the read interface.
Query the library health indicator and record its value.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Health indicator reports healthy while fresh samples flow and reports unhealthy after the staleness threshold is exceeded with no fresh samples.

test_cases.title: Read Failure Returns Failure Status
test_cases.setup: Initialize the library with a POSIX mock device that can be configured to inject I/O failures on the next read call.
procedure: Configure the mock device to return an I/O error on the next read.
Invoke the library read interface and capture the returned status code.
Reset the mock to nominal behavior and invoke the library read interface again.
Capture the second returned status code.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: First read returns a non-success JUNO_STATUS_T failure code; second read returns JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS, demonstrating recovery and explicit failure reporting.

test_cases.title: Non-Blocking Read Honors Timeout
test_cases.setup: Initialize the library with a POSIX mock device configured to delay sample availability beyond the caller-supplied timeout. Use a mocked clock to measure elapsed time.
procedure: Configure the mock device so that no sample is available within the next 100 ms of mocked time.
Call the library read interface with a timeout of 10 ms; record start and end mocked-clock timestamps and the returned status.
Configure the mock device so that a fresh sample is available immediately.
Call the library read interface with a timeout of 10 ms; record start and end mocked-clock timestamps and the returned status.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Timed-out call returns within 10 ms +/- 1 ms of mocked elapsed time with a timeout/no-data status; available-sample call returns success in less than 10 ms; neither call blocks past the timeout.

test_cases.title: POSIX Implementation API Equivalence
test_cases.setup: Build the baro_lib_test target against the POSIX implementation. The test fixture exercises the public library API only. A pre-recorded reference dataset of Pico2-build outputs for an enumerated set of injected pressure, temperature, and altitude inputs is available to the test as a fixture file.
procedure: Initialize the library via the public New/Init API on the POSIX build.
Inject the enumerated mock pressure, temperature, and altitude values via the POSIX device shim, matching the inputs used to produce the Pico2 reference dataset.
Invoke each public API entry point: read sample, query health, query POST result.
Capture each entry point's returned status code and the populated output structure fields (pressure, temperature, altitude, health, POST result).
Verify each entry point returns a JUNO_STATUS_T and populates the same output structures defined in the public header.

Compare each captured POSIX output value (pressure, temperature, altitude) against the recorded Pico2 reference output for the same injected inputs; assert byte-for-byte equality of populated structure fields.
Compare each captured POSIX status code against the recorded Pico2 reference status code for the same call; assert equality.
Tear down the library via its public destructor.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Each API entry point on POSIX produces output values byte-equivalent to those produced by the Pico2 build for identical injected mock pressure, temperature, and altitude values; status codes match per call; no entry point returns success without populating the output structure with the injected values.

test_cases.title: Pico2 Hardware Sample Acquisition
test_cases.setup: Flight Pico 2 board with MPL3115A2 altimeter wired to the configured I2C bus. Firmware built with the Pico2 baro_lib implementation. Serial console open at 115200 baud.
procedure: Power on the flight board with the altimeter connected.
Wait for POST to complete and the application loop to begin.
Capture at least 30 seconds of serial output containing periodic baro sample logs (pressure, temperature, altitude).
Apply a known stimulus by lifting the board approximately 1 meter and lowering it.
Confirm the altitude field in the serial log responds to the stimulus.
Save the captured serial log to file.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Serial log shows continuous baro samples at the configured cadence; pressure stays within plausible local atmospheric range; altitude field changes by approximately 1 m during the lift stimulus.

expected_artifacts.name: pico2_baro_serial.log
expected_artifacts.description: Serial capture of Pico2 firmware logging baro samples during the lift stimulus

test_cases.title: Sample Rate Sustained Under Read Errors
test_cases.setup: Initialize the library with a POSIX mock device. Mock clock advances in 50 ms steps. Configure the mock to inject one I/O failure every tenth read.
procedure: Run the read interface in a loop for 4 seconds of mocked time at 50 ms cadence (80 calls).
Record each call's returned status and timestamp.
Count successful reads and failed reads.
Verify successful reads continue at 20 Hz cadence aside from the injected failures.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Approximately 72 successful reads and 8 failed reads recorded; successful reads maintain 50 ms +/- 1 ms cadence; failed reads return non-success status without stalling subsequent calls.

test_cases.title: Health Reflects POST Failure at Startup
test_cases.setup: Initialize the library with a POSIX mock device configured to fail the device probe (whoami/identification) during initialization.
procedure: Configure the mock device so the POST probe returns a non-responsive result.
Initialize the library via its New/Init entry point.
Query the library POST result.
Query the library health indicator immediately after initialization.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: POST result reports device absent or non-responsive; health indicator reports unhealthy; subsequent read calls return failure status without crashing.
